construct: Classical random measurement error in a continuous exposure variable attenuates the estimated exposure-outcome association toward the null in simple regression, a phenomenon known as regression dilution or attenuation bias.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: A single noisy measurement of a continuous exposure used as a proxy for the true long-term exposure introduces classical measurement error; in simple regression this attenuates the estimated association toward zero, i.e. regression dilution.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Confounding, immortal time, and outcome-based selection require different causal/design structures. Random exposure error also does not improve precision.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The stem explicitly states random day-to-day exposure measurement error and simple regression, the assumptions under which attenuation toward the null is the canonical result.
